message.content:
The product of the first 20 positive integers is \(20!\).

For a number to be relatively prime to \(20!\), it must have no prime factor in common with \(20!\). The prime factors of \(20!\) are all primes up to 20:

\[
2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19
\]

So the smallest integer greater than 1 that is relatively prime to \(20!\) must not be divisible by any of these primes.

Checking numbers just above 1, all numbers from 2 through 20 share a prime factor with \(20!\). The next integer is:

\[
23
\]

Since \(23\) is prime and greater than 20, it is not among the prime factors of \(20!\), so \(\gcd(23,20!)=1\).

The answer is 23.
